A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpatialScore, SpatialCorpus, and SpatialAgent study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding figures, tables, equations, and supplementary material can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, supervised fine-tuning and SpatialAgent experiments in Tables 2–3, with additional quantitative results and case studies in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports specialist-model evaluations, few-shot comparisons, and computational measurements in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The supervised fine-tuning procedure, Plan-Execute and ReAct workflows, and spatial toolbox remain unchanged. The appendix training settings, agent prompts, and tool specifications match. Few-shot prompting is added as a comparison setting, not a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain SpatialScore's 5,025 examples across 30 tasks and SpatialCorpus's 330,802 training examples across 16 tasks, with the same source datasets and modality types. Revised modality counts and additional prompting settings do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands specialist comparisons with SpatialThinker-3B/7B, VST-3B/7B in SFT and RL variants, Spatial-MLLM-4B, and SpatialReasoner-8B: eight added configurations, with none removed. Table 3 also adds one-, two-, and four-shot Qwen3-VL comparisons for both model sizes.

E3.justification: v3 adds one-, two-, and four-shot evaluation using randomly selected, pre-allocated category examples, plus tool profiling with Qwen3-VL-8B under Plan-Execute. Table 5 revises single-/multi-image counts from 2,826/1,006 to 2,493/1,339; this does not establish dataset replacement or rerunning. Existing accuracy/MRA scoring, frame budgets, and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a focused analysis of performance with different numbers of in-context examples. Appendix B.3 and new Table 6 examine inference overhead and tool invocation frequency. Existing failure-rate analyses, subset comparisons, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies that the human baseline averages the scores of the already-described three PhD evaluators. This clarifies statistical aggregation without establishing additional evaluations. Fixed-seed and deterministic model evaluation practices remain unchanged, with no added confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 2 results make VST-3B-RL (48.04) and VST-7B-RL (52.47) their groups' leaders. Table 3 adds few-shot results, including four-shot scores of 46.59/49.00 for 4B/8B. Appendix B.3 newly reports 0.9/5.4/9.3 seconds per sample for base/Plan-Execute/ReAct and per-tool costs. This substantially expands reported findings; shared accuracy values and appendix subset results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation and agent equations (1–8) are unchanged, as is the appendix MRA scoring formula. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, training-corpus, and training-free agent contributions remain unchanged, as do claims about persistent spatial-intelligence limitations. The abstract and conclusion update the reported evaluation count from 40 to 49 models, reflecting expanded supporting evidence rather than a new central claim.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 qualifies the earlier characterization of spatial fine-tuning by explicitly recognizing VST's substantial improvements. Appendix B.3 adds a practical feasibility explanation based on CPU offloading and single-A100 execution. The existing limitations concerning RGB inputs, training-data coverage, and tool reliability remain.

D1.justification: v3 discloses five curation volunteers, an intermediate pool of 8,793 samples, and selection criteria. Appendix B clarifies identical baseline prompts, OpenCV-assisted human evaluation, and GPU/CPU deployment details. The title page adds checkpoint and SpatialCorpus access links. These are documentation and access additions, without evidence of changed underlying training or agent procedures.

R1.justification: Seven references are added: Cosmos, SpatialThinker, VersaViT, LAMRA, Satori-R1, SVQA-R1, and OmniStream. These modestly broaden the research context without restructuring the paper's positioning. Publication-venue updates for existing references do not represent additional cited works.

P1.justification: There are localized additions to curation, evaluation, and efficiency explanations, along with cross-reference wording and affiliation edits. The section hierarchy, overall narrative, and most existing prose remain intact; there is no extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 expand to accommodate new comparisons, and a computational-overhead table is introduced as Table 6. Existing appendix Tables 6–7 become Tables 7–8 and relocate. Figures retain their content, with surrounding material reflowing within the same overall visual design.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens comparative evidence through specialist baselines and few-shot controls, appropriately qualifies its fine-tuning interpretation to acknowledge VST, and exposes inference costs in Appendix B.3. Clearer curation details and resource links also improve reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains; the benchmark, proposed methods, and retained experimental findings remain substantially unchanged.
